label_definitions.acceptable: A genuine test failure developers of that era would also have seen: a real assertion, logic, or behavioral failure in the project's OWN code. It legitimately reduces coverage and is valid signal.
label_definitions.problematic: An ENVIRONMENT / pipeline artifact, NOT the code's fault: network isolation, unresolved module/dependency, build/toolchain mismatch, temporal/clock drift, OOM/timeout, or missing system library. When genuinely ambiguous, DEFAULT to this label.
label_definitions.false_positive: NOT a real failure: e.g. a passing run aborted by jest console-output capture, benign warnings that fail the run, or a coverage-threshold-only exit. The tests effectively passed.

system: You are a judge that classifies a single test-run failure from a longitudinal code-coverage pipeline. Output strict JSON only. You MUST pick exactly one label; never refuse or output 'unclear'.
